chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from some of our companions, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both), that he said:
"A man is not compelled except to provide for the maintenance of his parents and his children."

I said to Jamil, 'And what about the wife?' He said, 'Our companions have narrated from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both) that he said: "If he clothes her with what covers her private parts and feeds her with what sustains her strength, she remains with him; otherwise, he divorces her."'
I said to Jamil, 'Is he compelled to provide for the maintenance of his sister?' He said, 'If he were compelled to provide for his sister, that would be contrary to the narration.'
ai.seo_question: What are the specific financial maintenance obligations of a man towards his parents, wife, and children according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* delineates the scope of compulsory financial maintenance (*nafaqah*) in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing between mandatory support for parents and children and the conditional nature of spousal support. It highlights the scholarly consensus that while a husband must provide sufficient clothing and food to sustain his wife, failure to do so grants her the right to separation, whereas supporting a sister remains non-compulsory to avoid contradicting established legal precedents. This distinction underscores the principle of *ikrah* (legal compulsion) being limited to specific kinship ties as derived from the Imams.
